findings.claim: Every task2Students failure, and the task4EnrollmentKeys failures on the student inserts, now print the test's insert, which contains OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE (SchemaTest.java lines 71, 80, 83-84 print the SQL; lines 119, 150-157, 182, 192 contain the clause). README line 91 tells learners the failure shows 'the test's insert', but neither the README nor the module lessons explain this clause; create-table-data-types-and-constraints/artifact.md line 107 only mentions GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. A novice who sees an unfamiliar clause in the failing statement may think their schema must provide or support it, or may copy a shorter insert without the clause into psql and get a different result against a GENERATED ALWAYS id. Per the PostgreSQL 18 INSERT documentation (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html, retrieved 2026-10-14), a GENERATED ALWAYS column rejects an explicit value unless OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE or OVERRIDING USER VALUE is given.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to the README Task 2 Expect line or the Test section, for example: 'The tests' student inserts include OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE so they can supply fixed ids even if you make students.id an identity column; you do not need to write this clause, and it changes nothing for a plain whole-number id.' Do not change the test behaviour.

items.note: Still resolved on the current bytes after commit ebefad366a63ea2924c0be8f56377fe0c3fe8a76, which only adds OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE to the student inserts (lines 119, 150-157, 182, 192) and leaves all assertions, accepted type sets and SQLSTATE sets unchanged. This widens accepted designs: the module's own lesson (create-table-data-types-and-constraints/artifact.md line 107) points learners at GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, which the f631bff3 tests rejected with 'cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value' (lab-run.json variantRuns). PostgreSQL 18 INSERT docs (sql-insert.html, retrieved 2026-10-14) confirm the clause makes explicit values override GENERATED ALWAYS, does nothing for GENERATED BY DEFAULT, and that PostgreSQL 'allows the clause in any case and ignores it if it is not applicable', so plain integer and serial ids still pass; lab-run.json records exit 0 with 5/5 passing for integer, GENERATED BY DEFAULT and bigint GENERATED ALWAYS ids, and nonconforming identity schemas still fail only the matching criterion. The NULL-id check still yields 23502 because identity columns are implicitly NOT NULL. The README is unchanged (d52b0269...), still states only criteria and required identifiers, discloses no completed schema, and does not contradict the tests; learners never write the clause. Feedback stays criterion-labelled, with one low clarity gap recorded as sql-relational-edu-identity-001. This review did not run the tests locally because no PostgreSQL server was available; behaviour claims rely on the official docs and the recorded lab run.
